The rotated cube at 512³ — 134 million cells, sharp cut faces

Uniform flow past a 45°-rotated square prism at ReD = 1000, one flow-through. Spanwise vorticity ωz at the mid-plane, flow left to right. At D/h ≈ 64 cells across the body this is the finest cut-cell case run so far — the shear layers separating off the two upstream corners are resolved without a wall model.

On playback: the solver wrote 63 mid-plane slices (one every 0.1 box-time over the flow-through). These are motion-interpolated (optical-flow, ×3) to a smooth 60 fps loop — the underlying physics is 63 real snapshots at full 512² resolution, not 60 fps of raw data.

How it was solved

The body is an embedded cut-cell boundary on the staggered MAC grid: each face carries an open-area aperture weighting the divergence, pressure Poisson operator and gradient, so the wall is a sharp no-penetration condition rather than a stairstep of blocked cells.

That makes the pressure operator variable-coefficient, so it runs as an FFT-preconditioned conjugate gradient — the periodic FFT solve preconditions the apertured operator, which differs from it only at the body — converging in ~37 iterations/step. All CG scalars now live on-device, so each iteration costs a single 16-byte host round-trip instead of five.

FP32 fields, FP64 reductions, on an AMD RX 7900 XTX. 2622 steps at 1.77 s/step, ~77 min wall. Continuity held at max |div| ≈ 3×10⁻⁵ throughout.
